rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / CLASSES / CHAPTER 13

slides.title: Classes: methods and properties
slides.main: Your own objects start to behave like parts of the language.

items.title: Operators
items.sub: Plus, equals and comparison are methods

items.title: Containers
items.sub: len, indexing and in for your class

items.title: Properties
items.sub: A method that looks like an attribute

slides.title: Operators are methods
slides.main: An operator method returns a new object, it does not change the originals.

slides.title: Equality and hash
slides.main: Defined __eq__? Define __hash__ too, or the object can't be a dict key.

slides.title: Order and sorting
slides.main: With __lt__, sorted, min and max work without a key.

body.text: total_ordering from functools builds the other ordering operators.

slides.title: Your own container
slides.main: Want an object to act like a list? Implement the methods it needs.

slides.title: The property
slides.sub: A method that reads like an attribute
slides.main: What is stored is a way to get the value, not the value: always up to date.

slides.title: Setter and validation
slides.main: Outside, plain assignment; inside, a check; the value lives in _age.

slides.title: Class method
slides.main: Need another way to create an object? Write a class method “from something”.

slides.title: Static method
slides.sub: A function inside a class, for order
slides.main: A method knows the object, a class method the class, a static one nobody.

slides.title: Underscores in names
slides.main: Conventions, not locks: they keep code predictable for anyone who knows Python.

body.text:
class A:
    def __init__(self):
        self._internal = 1     # convention
        self.__mangled = 2     # name mangling

a = A()
print(a._internal)
print(a._A__mangled)
print(hasattr(a, "__mangled"))

slides.title: Example: a library
slides.sub: All together: str, len, comparison, property
slides.main: Code reads like a description of the domain: nothing extra.

slides.title: Typical mistakes
slides.main: An operator method returns a new object; in a setter, store in _name.

body.text: Also: property without a setter (AttributeError), setter recursion, self mixed up with cls.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Only the magic you need: implement just the methods you really use.
